headline: Bitcoin steadies near $83K after Trump rules out Iran strike, while XRP ETFs stand alone with inflows
summary: A geopolitical sigh of relief steadied Bitcoin near $82,966 after President Trump pledged to avoid an Iran military strike before the midterms — reducing one source of risk that had been weighing on the market. Most altcoins still slid, with BNB, Solana, and Dogecoin each falling roughly 2%, as ETF outflows from Bitcoin and Ethereum funds continued to drag on risk appetite. The standout exception was XRP, whose ETFs were the only crypto funds to record net inflows on the day.

winners.name: Bitway
winners.catalyst: No specific catalyst identified — the move appears technical on a day when most assets declined.

losers.name: Bitcoin Cash
losers.catalyst: Bitcoin Cash fell nearly 6% amid broad altcoin weakness as rising bond yields and oil prices added macro pressure. ETF outflow momentum from the prior session continued to weigh on risk appetite across non-BTC assets, and BCH had no specific positive catalyst to resist the selloff.

whyItMoved:
The day's main driver was a reduction in geopolitical risk. Trump's public pledge to avoid a military strike on Iran before the midterm elections eased one of the near-term fears that had been pushing traders toward the exits — and Bitcoin responded, climbing just under 1% to settle around $82,966. That kind of political statement doesn't change crypto's fundamentals, but it does remove a specific tail risk that markets had been pricing in.

The relief didn't extend far down the asset list. Rising bond yields and higher oil prices kept macro pressure on risk assets broadly, and most altcoins in the top 15 finished lower. BNB fell 2.32%, Solana dropped 1.88%, Dogecoin slid 2.43%, and Monero lost 2.26%. These moves tracked the broader pattern of the prior session, where ETF outflows from Bitcoin and Ethereum funds had already signaled cooling institutional appetite.

XRP was a notable exception — not in price (it slipped 0.42%), but in fund flows. XRP ETFs were the only crypto investment products to record net inflows on the day, even as Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Zcash funds all saw redemptions. That divergence points to continued institutional demand for XRP-specific exposure, separate from the broader market direction.

Zcash gained 1.31%, the strongest move among top-15 non-stablecoin assets. Developers announced a January target for quantum-resistant payment capabilities — a concrete technical milestone that likely attracted fresh attention to ZEC on an otherwise down day for altcoins.

The Fear & Greed index sits at 59, in "Greed" territory, though the day's action suggests that reading may soften if macro headwinds persist.
worthKnowing: Thailand's SEC issued formal rules enabling domestic Bitcoin and Ether ETF listings, effective October 16 — expanding regulated crypto investment access in Southeast Asia.
The UK government sanctioned three crypto exchanges, including Cryptomus and TokenSpot, over alleged ties to Russia-linked transactions.
Zcash developers set a January deadline for quantum-resistant payment capabilities following what they described as a 'bunker mode' security scare.
